$comment: Generated from game/src/pack/adventure.ts by `npm run pack:schema`. Do not edit by hand.

$schema.description: For editors: the path or URL of this schema.

_comment.description: A note for people editing the file; the game ignores it.

licence.description: The pack's licence, e.g. CC-BY-4.0. A committed pack carries only our own or CC-BY text.

items.description: A file path relative to the pack folder.

prose.description: Adventure-wide prose: premise, the truth behind it, tone.

lore.description: Setting text the DM reads, possibly shared with other packs (paths may leave the pack).

items.description: A file path relative to the pack folder.

_comment.description: A note for people editing the file; the game ignores it.

handle.description: The character's creature handle in the first scene's file.

seat.description: Who plays it by default: the human, or an AI player agent.

card.description: Its personality card (CHR-5): the only character text in an AI player's prompt besides its sheet.

names.description: What the table calls the character, every form of it: its name in each language and each case («Торва», «Торве», «Торву»). A line that names an AI player gives it the floor first (party talk §4.2); its handle and its card's name always count.

pronouns.description: How the table refers to the character, such as she/her (M7 design §3.4): the DM's prompt names it, and the narration check holds the DM to it.

name_ru.description: The one Russian form the agents write in a Russian run (AGT-38), such as «Ильза»; it must be among `names`.

party.description: The party, in seat order. The first scene's file places them.

_comment.description: A note for people editing the file; the game ignores it.

name_ru.description: What a Russian run calls them (AGT-38), such as «староста Осрик Хейл».

prose.description: Who they are, voice, wants, what they know and tell, what they hide.

stat_block.description: An entry of `stat_blocks` (format 2): what the NPC fights as when the story turns violent and the scene doesn't place them, such as town_guard. The DM brings them in with place_creature under that entry (MON-11).

creatures.description: When the NPC is also an engine creature (it can be fought, talked down or captured): the scene and handle it has. Several entries when any one of them may become the NPC, such as whichever goblin surrenders.

scene.description: A scene id of this skeleton.

handle.description: A creature in that scene's file, its spawns included.

glossary_ru.description: How a Russian run says the pack's words that a model translates badly (AGT-85), keyed by the English word in the prose: "oilskin coat": "промасленный плащ". Only the DM's Russian prompt carries it; the skeleton is DM-only.

anchors_ru.description: What a Russian seat calls each scene anchor, by anchor id (AGT-98): "the_well": "колодец". The engine sends anchors' English names; the seat reads these instead in a Russian run. One name per id across the pack's scenes.

glyphs.description: One glyph per creature kind for the turn-order line of the human's panel (M10 P7, AGT-67), keyed by a party handle or by a creature's kind as the panel names it ("Goblin Warrior"). Each is one grapheme, such as one emoji. The bar shows it in front of the handle; the roster never does.

stat_blocks.description: The only creatures the DM may place beyond the scene files (format 2 and later). Empty: the DM improvises no creatures.

_comment.description: A note for people editing the file; the game ignores it.

id.description: What the DM names in place_creature, such as road_bandit. DM-only, like the stat block id.

monster.description: A stat block id in the engine's registry, as in a scene file's `monster` (`wolf`, or a namespaced id).

side.description: Which side of a fight it is on. The engine refuses a side its stat block can't take beside the party.

name.description: What the table calls the creature instead of the stat block's name, such as Grey wolf.

carries.description: Coin and items each such creature carries, taken by loot once it falls or surrenders. Authored here, never by the DM; DM-only until looted.

item.description: An item id as on a sheet, such as potion_of_healing.

items.description: A creature the DM may bring in when a story beat needs one the scene file doesn't hold (API-33, AGT-24).

_comment.description: A note for people editing the file; the game ignores it.

id.description: The engine scene id: `scenes/<id>.json` in the pack.

target_minutes.description: The scene's share of the run (scope §3).

prose.description: Read-aloud opening, what the characters can notice, how to run it.

_comment.description: A note for people editing the file; the game ignores it.

check.description: A check id in the scene's file.

intent.description: The kind of thing a character says or does that this check answers.

items.description: Which engine check fits which player intent. Anything else the DM checks from the SRD DC ladder.

_comment.description: A note for people editing the file; the game ignores it.

encounter.description: An encounter id in the scene's file.

rest.description: The DM offers a Short Rest here. Leaving the scene while the party is hurt and nobody rested in it reminds the DM once.

_comment.description: A note for people editing the file; the game ignores it.

to.description: The scene it loads: a scene id of this skeleton.

when.description: What ends the scene this way.

carry.description: Who goes along: the party, or the party and any creature that surrendered to it.

items.description: A way out of a scene.

scenes.description: In play order; the first places the party, every later one carries it in.

world.description: A living-world pack's campaign.json only (MAP-7): the engine's world block (map, start, hour, caravan, route, road_scene, scenes, escort). The engine reads and checks it; the game reads only start and scenes. Its scenes need no exits: the road joins them.

day_limit.description: A living-world pack only: the last game day a run plays; the night after it ends the run.

description: A scenario pack's skeleton (M6 spec §4). DM-only, like the prose and scene files.
